bug_semantics: mac802154 treats local->interfaces (historically priv->slaves) as an RCU list: adds use list_add_tail_rcu(), single-interface removal uses list_del_rcu()+synchronize_rcu(), and ieee802154_wake_queue()/stop_queue()/disable_queue() walk the list under rcu_read_lock() with list_for_each_entry_rcu(). Bulk hardware teardown (ieee802154_remove_interfaces, originally the loop in ieee802154_unregister_device/unregister_hw) instead called list_del(), which poisons list_head next/prev (LIST_POISON*). An in-flight async xmit completion can therefore follow a poisoned node in ieee802154_wake_queue() (inlined from ieee802154_release_queue), producing a KASAN wild-memory-access/GPF at dead000000000218. Local CAP_NET_ADMIN in a user namespace can race AF_IEEE802154 sendmmsg against MAC802154_HWSIM_CMD_DEL_RADIO / driver unregister; the 2026 fix changes only the bulk path to list_del_rcu() and relies on the subsequent unregister_netdevice() RCU wait rather than an extra synchronize_rcu().
flaw_origin: The defective writer was introduced in 62610ad21870a8cf842d4a48f07c3a964e1d2622 (mac802154: slaves management support, 2012-05-16, v3.5-rc1). That commit first added the bulk teardown loop in ieee802154_unregister_device() that does list_del(&sdata->list) on the same list it already managed with list_add_tail_rcu() and list_del_rcu() on the single-iface path. Immediate parent 90c049b2c6ae26d1a4d526d660a976620eaa554a has ieee802154_unregister_device() with no list walk and no list_del anywhere under net/mac802154/. The 2014 Fixes: commit 592dfbfc72f5352437c883aa11ab579d10cdb595 only relocates that unchanged list_del() loop from net/mac802154/main.c into ieee802154_remove_interfaces() in iface.c (a move, not a BIC). CNA git ranges that start at 592dfbfc72f5/v3.19 follow that Fixes tag mechanically.

reasoning: CVE-2026-72024 is a published Linux CNA record (not withdrawn/rejected) for an RCU list poison in mac802154 bulk interface teardown. syzbot and the patch all identify the crash as ieee802154_wake_queue() following a list_del()-poisoned local->interfaces node during async TX completion; the actual code change is list_del -> list_del_rcu in ieee802154_remove_interfaces(), with unregister_netdevice() providing the RCU wait. That is a real use-after-free-class kernel memory-corruption bug, so the case is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The Fixes: SHA 592dfbfc72f5352437c883aa11ab579d10cdb595 is the first surviving blame hit on the iface.c line, but its subject, diff, and parent main.c copy show a pure move of an already-vulnerable list_del() loop out of ieee802154_unregister_hw(); protocol forbids treating a move as BIC. git log -S and the 2012 patch show the smallest first-write is 62610ad21870a8cf842d4a48f07c3a964e1d2622, which added the bulk list_del() while already using RCU list add/delete on the sibling paths; the line is absent in parent 90c049b2c6ae26d1a4d526d660a976620eaa554a. Later RCU walkers (monitor RX the same day, netif flow-control in 2013, wake/stop helpers in 2014) complete the race the CVE describes but did not first write the defective deletion. The BIC is a 2012 human commit by Alexander Smirnov committed by David S. Miller with only Signed-off-by trailers and no commit-object AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
